_comment: Session checkpoint policy — guarantees a SESSION FILE ON DISK AT ALL TIMES (user requirement 2026-06-12: 'WE MUST HAVE A SESSION FILE IN DISK'). Two complementary layers: (1) the hibernate image in the swapfile carries the full RAM session, but only exists from hibernate events and is consumed on resume; (2) THIS — periodic read-only btrfs snapshots of the home subvolume. Apps persist their own session state into home continuously (browser sessionstore, editor autosaves, KDE config, tmux), so a home snapshot IS a recoverable session checkpoint that survives shutdown, crash, and firmware power-cut. CoW snapshots cost ~0 bytes until files diverge. Consumed by configuration_session-checkpoint.nix.
_enabled_comment: Turned OFF 2026-08-11 by explicit request ('remove all snapshots i dont need them'). The premise above — 'CoW snapshots cost ~0 bytes until files diverge' — is true on day one and false by day three, and that gap is what broke disk protection on this box: three @home-diego checkpoints (oldest 8 Aug) PINNED every extent the reclaim ladder deleted, so purge_tmp_*, purge_audit_old, docker_prune_*, dev_store_gc and purge_octocode_stale all freed ~0 bytes, recheck_gate correctly concluded 'reclaim insufficient', and the emergency tier escalated to FREEZE + SIGTERM workload.slice — twice, on 2026-08-11. Deleting 4.9G of stale octocode index moved the pool 0%. Only /nix escaped, because @nixos/nix is not in the checkpoint set. enabled=false stops the timer and the shutdown/hibernate units (lib.mkIf enabled in configuration_session-checkpoint.nix); it does NOT delete snapshots that already exist — those need a root `btrfs subvolume delete`. Re-enabling means accepting that reclaim cannot free space held by a checkpoint.

checkpoint._comment: btrfs_root must be the mounted pool top-level. source_subvol is snapshotted READ-ONLY into snapshot_dir/<UTC-timestamp>. Nested subvolumes (e.g. container storage inside home) are automatically excluded by btrfs — desirable, they are not session state. interval_minutes drives the periodic systemd timer; retention_count is a simple newest-N prune. CADENCE (2026-06-27): the periodic timer is a slow safety net (every 6h) — the session-relevant moments are covered by EVENT checkpoints instead: shutdown_checkpoint (every reboot/shutdown) and hibernate_checkpoint (every hibernate trigger). No need for a sub-hour periodic timer. retention_count=3 (HARD CAP — user 2026-07-08: 'keep only 3 snapshots, not more'). WHY NOT 1: retention_count=1 lost a real session — a fresh boot's periodic checkpoint (fires 5min after boot) pruned the previous session's snapshot before it could be recovered, so after any crash/reboot you could NEVER roll back the prior session (the recovery boot itself deleted it). Keeping the newest 3 guarantees the previous session survives at least one reboot (its shutdown/periodic checkpoints stay among the newest 3). TRADEOFF: each RETAINED older snapshot pins the OLD copy of any extent later changed/deleted in @home-diego, so 3 snapshots hold a bounded window of churn (deleted caches, build output) — CoW keeps this ~0 until files diverge; 3 is the accepted ceiling. Do NOT raise above 3 without weighing pool pressure.
checkpoint._notify_comment: When true, each PERIODIC checkpoint pops a desktop notification (notify-send, follows the KDE dark theme) confirming the local snapshot was saved. Shutdown checkpoints never notify (session is ending). Set false for silent operation.

shutdown_checkpoint._comment: REBOOT/SHUTDOWN MUST ALWAYS SAVE A SNAPSHOT IN DISK (user requirement 2026-06-12, hard). In addition to the periodic timer, a final btrfs checkpoint is written on the way down — every reboot and every shutdown, before filesystems unmount. Apps flush their session stores (browser tabs, editor state, KDE session) when the session ends, so this snapshot captures the freshest possible file-state of the session being closed.

hibernate_checkpoint._comment: HIBERNATE MUST ALSO SAVE A BTRFS SNAPSHOT (2026-06-27). Hibernate does NOT pass through shutdown.target, so session-checkpoint-shutdown never fires on a hibernate trigger — the file-checkpoint gap. This wires session-checkpoint-hibernate Before=systemd-hibernate.service (the unit every hibernate path funnels through: manual `systemctl hibernate`, the battery-watchdog critical hibernate, and `reboot-with-session`), so a fresh file snapshot lands just before the RAM image is written. Bounded by a short TimeoutStartSec in the .nix so a stuck snapshot can never block a battery-critical hibernate.

reboot_with_session._comment: `sudo reboot-with-session` — the RAM-session counterpart for restarts: writes the FULL hibernate image to the swapfile, then REBOOTS (kernel disk-mode 'reboot') instead of powering off. At the rEFInd menu that follows: NixOS - Primary (default) resumes the saved session; NixOS - Fresh Desktop starts clean and discards it. Implemented via a runtime /run/systemd/sleep.conf.d drop-in (HibernateMode=reboot) that exists only for this invocation — /run is tmpfs, so a completed reboot wipes it and the battery-watchdog's critical hibernate keeps normal power-off semantics. Use plain Restart or Fresh Desktop when booting a NEW kernel is the point (resuming the image returns to the old one by design).

restore._comment: How to use a checkpoint. Single file: plain copy out of the snapshot path (read-only, browsable like a normal directory). Full home rollback: boot a rescue entry, `mv @home-diego @home-diego.broken && btrfs subvolume snapshot /mnt/btrfs-root/@snapshots/home-diego/<ts> /mnt/btrfs-root/@home-diego` (writable snapshot-of-snapshot), reboot.

testers._comment: Run via test-session-checkpoint.sh (same data-driven runner pattern as test-hibernation.sh).

checks.description: at least one checkpoint snapshot exists on disk
retention is capped at 3 — never more than 3 checkpoints on disk (user hard cap 2026-07-08; prevents the KEEP=1 bug that pruned the previous session on a fresh boot)
newest checkpoint is a read-only btrfs snapshot (immutable session file)
checks.command: btrfs property get "/mnt/btrfs-root/@snapshots/home-diego/$(ls -1 /mnt/btrfs-root/@snapshots/home-diego/ | sort | tail -1)" ro

checks.description: session-checkpoint-shutdown is wired into shutdown.target — every reboot/shutdown writes a final snapshot (full proof appears in the journal of the NEXT boot as a '-shutdown' suffixed checkpoint)
reboot-with-session command is installed (RAM-session snapshot + reboot)
session-checkpoint-hibernate is wired Before=systemd-hibernate.service — every hibernate trigger writes a btrfs snapshot first
periodic timer cadence is 6h (360min) — the slow safety net; event checkpoints (shutdown/hibernate) cover the session-relevant moments
checkpoint service runs idle IO class — can never trash the interactive session (systemd reports the class numerically: 3 = idle)
